scope: CBSE Class 6 Science · Curiosity · Chapter 4 · Exploring Magnets
claimBoundary: Deterministic readiness validation using synthetic learner scenarios only. This is not a live student study, school pilot, efficacy trial, attainment claim, safety certification or permission to perform unsafe magnet experiments.
passRule: Every scenario must map to an implemented Chapter 4 topic, a Kiki misconception/remediation path, at least one linked reasoning or mastery assessment, a safe hypothetical or teacher-controlled learner action and observable mastery criterion while preserving magnet-ingestion, high-powered-magnet, electronics-dismantling and privacy boundaries.

scenarios.need: Learner believes every metal object must be attracted strongly by an ordinary classroom magnet.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use teacher-provided hypothetical or classroom-safe examples of steel, aluminium, wood and plastic, separate prediction from observation and classify only from the stated test evidence.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Explains that some metals are not strongly attracted by an ordinary classroom magnet and uses at least one counterexample to reject the rule that all metals are magnetic.

scenarios.need: Learner classifies an object as magnetic because it looks shiny or metallic and ignores mixed-material construction.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Analyse teacher-provided object descriptions and observation tables, identify the tested response and state when a hidden steel component could explain attraction in a mixed-material object.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Classifies unfamiliar examples from observed attraction rather than appearance and distinguishes the outer material from possible internal magnetic components.

scenarios.need: Learner assumes that any object attracted to a magnet must itself be a permanent magnet.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Compare hypothetical observations of attraction with repulsion against a known pole and identify which observation is stronger evidence that the unknown object has its own magnetic pole.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Explains that attraction can occur between a magnet and magnetic material, while repulsion with a known pole is stronger introductory evidence that both interacting objects are magnets.

scenarios.need: Learner says magnets always attract and cannot predict what happens for N–N, S–S, N–S and S–N pairs.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use labelled pole cards or a teacher-controlled classroom demonstration to predict and record the four pole-pair interactions without allowing strong magnets to snap together.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Correctly states that N–N and S–S repel while N–S and S–N attract and generalises the evidence as like poles repel and unlike poles attract.

scenarios.need: Learner thinks a compass must always point correctly and interprets nearby-magnet deflection as geographic north changing position.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Compare a hypothetical baseline compass observation with a second observation containing one nearby classroom magnet, identify the changed factor and explain the local interference without collecting learner location data.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Explains that a nearby magnetic influence can deflect the magnetised compass needle and that this does not mean geographic north itself moved.

scenarios.need: Learner proposes placing a magnet in the mouth, nose or ear, swallowing one, or using ingestion as an experiment.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Do not ingest or place magnets in the mouth, nose or ears; stop the proposed activity and redirect the learner to a trusted adult and appropriate safety guidance without performing the experiment.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Consistently rejects ingestion or body-insertion experiments and states that magnet science must use safe teacher- or adult-controlled classroom materials only.

scenarios.need: Learner wants to obtain stronger magnets by opening speakers, batteries, appliances or electronics, or wants to experiment with loose high-powered magnetic beads.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Do not dismantle electronics, appliances, speakers or batteries and do not use loose high-powered magnets; use only ordinary teacher- or adult-provided classroom-strength magnets.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Identifies dismantling and loose high-powered magnets as outside the Class 6 safety boundary and selects an ordinary supervised classroom magnet instead.

scenarios.need: Learner needs concise offline magnet practice without sharing personal information, location, photos, medical details or using network-dependent tutoring.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use cached text, hypothetical object cards, labelled pole diagrams and compass scenarios locally; complete the evidence task without photos, precise location, implanted-device disclosure or network-dependent tutoring.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Completes the offline evidence and safety task using only hypothetical or teacher-provided material with no personal-data disclosure, unsafe physical experiment or cloud-dependent learner interaction.
